chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'If you disclose your charitable expenditures, it is good,' he said: 'He means the obligatory Zakat.'
I said: 'And if you conceal it and give it to the poor?' He said: 'He means the voluntary charity.'
Indeed, they used to prefer the manifestation of the obligatory duties and the concealment of the voluntary ones.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between obligatory Zakat and voluntary charity in Shia jurisprudence according to the Quranic exegesis?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the exegetical distinction between the obligatory Zakat and voluntary Sadaqah, attributing the preference for public display of the former to its role in social encouragement and the concealment of the latter to preserving sincerity (ikhlas). It reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that the Quranic praise for both modes applies to their respective categories, aligning with the Imams' practical guidance on maximizing communal benefit versus personal spiritual purity. This interpretation underscores the nuanced application of Quranic verses in juristic practice, distinguishing between ritual obligation and supererogatory devotion.
